- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.

- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

message.content: webhook dispatcher, billing-api, notifier, resizer, scheduler, search-indexer
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Which services does Dune own now?" Today is 2026-06-30.

Let me trace ownership of each service mentioned:

1. Reporting service: [2025-01-20] Dune owns reporting service. But [2025-11-07] handover: reporting service moves from team Dune to Boreal. So Boreal owns it now. Not Dune.

2. Webhook dispatcher: [2026-03-04] remains a team Dune service. [2026-02-04] webhooks owned by Dune. [2025-07-04] correction: webhooks owner is Dune. So Dune owns webhooks/webhook dispatcher. Yes.

3. Billing-api: [2026-05-26] handover: billing-api now sits with Dune team. Boreal no longer owns it. So Dune owns billing-api now. Yes.

4. Notifier: [2025-06-19] Notifier new home: team Dune. No later change mentioned. Yes, Dune owns notifier.

5. Resizer / image resizer: [2025-01-20] resizer lives with Dune. [2025-04-29] Ember taking over image resizer from Dune. Then [2025-12-01] resizer new home: Dune team; Ember kept it until today. So now Dune owns resizer. Yes.

6. Catalog: [2025-03-20] pager rings Dune. But [2025-06-16] Boreal is taking over catalog from Dune effective today. So Boreal owns catalog now. Not Dune.

7. Scheduler: [2025-10-15] pager for scheduler rings Dune, not Atlas. No later transfer. So Dune owns scheduler. Yes.

8. Search-indexer: [2025-12-08] pager for indexer rings Dune, not Cinder. So Dune owns search-indexer. Yes.

Also "webhook dispatcher needs the event bus to work" — event bus is a dependency, not ownership.

So services Dune owns now (as of 2026-06-30):
- webhook dispatcher (webhooks)
- billing-api
- notifier
- resizer (image resizer)
- scheduler
- search-indexer

The rule says reply in one short line with just the value asked for. So a comma-separated list.
